title: Order Theory
body:
Notes on "Introduction to Lattices and Order" by B.A. Davey and H.A. Priestley. Definitions:
  • Partial Order: Let P be a set. A partial order on P is a binary relation <= such that for all x,y,z in P:
    • x <= x (reflexivity)
    • x <= y and y <= x => x = y (antisymmetry)
    • x <= y and y <= z => x <= z (transitivity)
    If the above conditions are met, then P is an ordered set or poset. Notation varies but typically P is shown as <P;<=>. Any set with an order "=" is called the discrete order. If condition 2 on any set Q is not met, but condition 1 and 3 are (<= is not antisymmetric) then <= is called a quasi-order or pre-order.
  • Comparability: If x !<= y and y !<= x, then x and y are not comparable. Comparability is denoted by ||.
Forming New Ordered Sets From Existing Ones: Any subset Q of a poset P gets its ordering from P. This is called an induced order.
